diseases.label: Black Rot
diseases.name: Black Rot
diseases.short_description: A bacterial disease of cabbage-family crops, widely regarded as one of the most important diseases of crucifers. It enters mainly through leaf margins and spreads through the plant's veins.
common_symptoms: Yellow, V-shaped lesions starting at the leaf margin and pointing toward the midrib
Veins inside lesions turn dark brown to black
Lesions dry out and become brown and papery as they age
Severely infected leaves wilt and drop; plants may be stunted
visual_signs: The 'V' shape with its wide end at the leaf edge is the most characteristic sign
Blackened veins visible when an infected leaf or stem is cut or held to light
possible_causes: Infected or contaminated seed and transplants (a major source of introduction)
Bacteria surviving in infected crop debris and in cruciferous weeds
Spread by splashing rain, overhead irrigation, workers and tools moving through wet plants
Warm, humid weather favours infection and spread
prevention: Use certified disease-free or hot-water-treated seed and healthy transplants
Rotate away from all cabbage-family crops for at least 2-3 years
Control cruciferous weeds (e.g. wild mustard) that can host the bacterium
Prefer drip irrigation; avoid overhead watering and working in wet fields
Clean tools and equipment between fields
general_management: Remove and destroy badly infected plants and leaves; do not compost them in production areas
Incorporate or remove crop residue promptly after harvest so it breaks down
Work in infected areas last to avoid carrying bacteria to healthy plants
Chemical options for bacterial diseases are limited and region-specific - ask a local extension officer before using any product
when_to_seek_expert_help: Symptoms are spreading quickly across the field
You suspect the disease came in on seed or transplants
You need laboratory confirmation or locally registered control options

diseases.label: Downy Mildew
diseases.name: Downy Mildew
diseases.pathogen: Hyaloperonospora species (oomycete, a water-mould - not a true fungus)
diseases.short_description: A disease caused by a water-mould that thrives in cool, moist conditions. It affects seedlings and mature plants of cabbage-family crops.
common_symptoms: Pale green to yellow, often angular patches on the upper leaf surface, limited by veins
White to greyish fluffy/downy growth on the underside of leaves beneath the patches
Patches later turn tan or brown and may merge
Seedlings can be severely damaged or killed
visual_signs: Check the leaf underside early in the morning: the downy growth is the key sign
Angular patches bounded by veins, rather than V-shaped lesions from the margin
possible_causes: Cool temperatures combined with long periods of leaf wetness (dew, fog, rain)
Spores spread by wind and water splash
Resting spores can survive in infected crop debris
Dense planting and poor air circulation
prevention: Space plants to improve airflow and allow leaves to dry quickly
Avoid overhead irrigation, or irrigate early so foliage dries during the day
Use resistant or tolerant varieties where available
Start with healthy transplants and rotate cabbage-family crops
general_management: Remove heavily infected leaves and seedlings
Improve ventilation in nurseries and greenhouses
Monitor closely during cool, wet spells when the disease spreads fastest
If fungicide use is being considered, follow locally registered recommendations from an extension service
when_to_seek_expert_help: Symptoms persist despite improving airflow and reducing leaf wetness
You need help choosing resistant varieties or registered control options

diseases.label: Bacterial spot rot
diseases.name: Bacterial Spot Rot
diseases.pathogen: Not specified by the dataset label. Bacterial leaf spot of crucifers is commonly associated with Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola, and soft rots with Pectobacterium species.
diseases.short_description: A broad category for bacterial leaf spots and rots. The exact bacterium is not identified, so treat it as a general 'bacterial spot / rot' finding rather than a single confirmed disease.
common_symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown, tan or dark
Spots may have a yellow halo and can merge into larger dead areas
In rot-type infections, tissue becomes soft, watery and may smell unpleasant
Damaged areas can become entry points for further decay
visual_signs: Soft, collapsing tissue (rot) rather than the dry V-shaped lesions typical of black rot
possible_causes: Bacteria introduced on seed, transplants or debris
Spread by rain splash, overhead irrigation and handling wet plants
Wounds from insects, hail or tools that let bacteria enter
Warm, wet conditions and poor drainage favour rots
prevention: Use clean seed and healthy transplants
Avoid overhead irrigation and handling plants while wet
Minimise wounding during cultivation and harvest
Rotate crops and remove crop debris
general_management: Remove and dispose of affected leaves and rotting plants away from the field
Sanitise tools after working with infected plants
Harvest and store produce dry and cool to limit post-harvest rot
Because the exact pathogen is uncertain, a laboratory diagnosis is the best basis for any further treatment decision
when_to_seek_expert_help: You need to know which bacterium is involved (lab diagnosis)
Rot is spreading into heads (curds) or storage
Large parts of the crop are affected

diseases.label: No disease
diseases.name: No Disease (Healthy)
diseases.short_description: The model did not find patterns of the three diseases it was trained on. This does not rule out other diseases, pests or nutrient problems that the model was never trained to recognise.
common_symptoms: Uniform green leaf colour without spots, lesions or downy growth
visual_signs: No V-shaped margin lesions, angular yellow patches, or water-soaked spots
prevention: Keep scouting regularly - early detection matters most
Maintain crop rotation, clean seed and good field hygiene
Water at the base of plants and allow foliage to dry
general_management: Continue routine monitoring, especially after rain or cool, wet periods
Re-check any plant that later shows unusual spots, wilting or discolouration
when_to_seek_expert_help: Plants show symptoms the app does not cover (pests, nutrient deficiency, other diseases)
The plant looks unhealthy despite a 'No disease' result
